analysis:
Only docs/architecture/inference.md changed (date bump, new GLM5Next verified-weight-hash paragraph near head lines 684-691, video frame-timing text near 818-821, new text near 884-903 and 1740-1759). Only base text was supplied for these units, and the patch excerpt is truncated, so I could not see the head text of the added paragraphs in full. No source or code changes are visible; documentation changes alone create no concrete security regression.

The new paragraph describes a security-relevant design change that code reviewers should check. The load reports the manifest aggregate (GLM5NextManagedLoad.verifiedArtifactSHA256), and the next coordinator-mode start registers that hash without re-reading weights while each file's device, inode, size, mtime and ctime stay unchanged (VerifiedWeightHashStore). This is a metadata-based cache of weight verification. It relates to A-004, T-012 and T-027, where an operator with write access to the model cache could replace weights and preserve metadata. A same-size in-place overwrite changes mtime, but an operator with root access could restore mtime. ctime cannot be set directly, but it can be affected by clock manipulation or by replacing the file via inode swap. The doc says the load verifies again before serving, which mitigates the weight-hash claim reported to the coordinator. This is a pre-existing threat class (operator self-reports the weight hash). The doc claims the mitigation, but the actual code in VerifiedWeightHashStore and ProviderLoop.verifiedGLM5NextWeightHash was not supplied, so I cannot verify it. A reviewer of the code PR should confirm that the store is integrity-protected (owner-only, HMAC or KEK-keyed), that a failure falls back to a full hash, and that the re-verification before serving cannot be skipped.

The video frame-timing change (average frame rate rather than constant-frame-rate-only) loosens the input contract in the GLM5NextProcessor. The doc says processor limits remain, with a decoded-frame cap of 512 MiB, so I found no regression in the documentation. The code needs a bounds check for variable-frame-rate videos and for the T-050 temporary-file exposure. I made no claim about unchanged code paths.
